title: sjtsk: Slovak S-JTSK (JTSK, JTSK03) ↔ ETRS89 transformations the official way
description:
Problem. Spatial data in Slovakia come in three coordinate systems: the cadastre in S-JTSK [JTSK] (EPSG:5514; results delivered to the cadastre must be in JTSK by ÚGKK regulation No. 300/2009 Coll., § 18(1), as amended), the national datasets — topographic database ZBGIS, elevation model DMR5, national forest maps — in S-JTSK [JTSK03] (EPSG:8353), and GNSS field data in ETRS89 or WGS 84. Forest stands, cadastral parcels, field surveys and national rasters can be compared only if all of them are transformed the same way. The official way is defined by ÚGKK: the Helmert transformation ETRS89 ↔ JTSK03 (EPSG 8365 / 8367) and the GKÚ grid JTSK03 ↔ JTSK (EPSG 8364); for work whose results go to the cadastre, the departmental transformation service RTS is binding (§ 2(10)).

State as of 23 November 2026 (computed on 3,978 points covering Slovakia and tested in QGIS; METHODOLOGY.md):

  • common GIS software does not apply the official transformation reliably — PROJ picks "the best available" operation, and that depends on the installation;
  • the same point given in ETRS89 or in WGS 84 ends up up to 1.36 m apart; the usual WGS 84 parameters are up to 1.69 m off the official result;
  • JTSK03 data are often taken as JTSK, although the two differ by up to 1.64 m;
  • QGIS 3.44.12 (PROJ 9.8.1, Windows) transforms ETRS89 → EPSG:5514 with the Czech parameters "S-JTSK to ETRS89 (1)", off the official ÚGKK chain by up to 4.2 m (mean 1.9 m; 3.1–4.2 m in eastern Slovakia), confirmed in QGIS on 12 test points; installing the GKÚ grid alone does not change this choice.

All figures are differences from the official chain as defined in EPSG and implemented in PROJ — a comparison of models on computed points. Checked against the binding RTS service of ÚGKK on 56 points: the GKÚ grid step agrees to the rounding of the RTS output; the Helmert step differs by a constant 5.3 mm (the EPSG pair 8365/8367 itself does not close on a round trip, 10.6 mm); QGIS 3.44's default operation is 1.91 m off RTS on average and up to 4.10 m.

Solution. This library implements the official ÚGKK chain with the GKÚ grid included, so the result does not depend on how PROJ is installed (equal to PROJ with the official grid to below 0.01 mm); one path for ETRS89 and WGS 84; JTSK03 recognised and transformed, also when written as LOCAL_CS (DMR5); the variant is always explicit (converter(src, dst, "sk4") to compare or to match old data). The QGIS plugin S-JTSK Official Transformation brings the same transformation to QGIS and sets it as QGIS's preferred one.

Aim. Forest stand boundaries, cadastral parcels, GNSS field data and national rasters in Slovakia should match at the level of the official transformation (millimetres) regardless of the software and its installation — with an open, reproducible method that others can check and reuse.
